title: EXPLAIN BUFFERS: cache vs disk
claim: "shared hit" is data found in cache, "shared read" came from disk. If most pages are read, the working set
does not fit in memory. A query served from cache can be 100x faster than one hitting disk.
verdict: Confirmed, with nuance. The small query (7.5k pages) read everything on its first run
({first:small_working_set}), then found all pages in the 128 MB cache ({t:small_working_set}). The large one
needs 69.5k pages (550 MB): it read them on every run ({t:large_working_set}) and pushed everything else out of
shared_buffers. Those reads mostly came from the OS page cache (16 GB RAM); from the disk itself they would be
slower. shared_buffers is at the 128 MB default: raising it (e.g. 4 GB) is the cheapest win on this machine.

sections.label: shared_buffers afterwards: the large query pushed other pages out
sections.sql:
SELECT c.relname, count(*) AS buffers, pg_size_pretty(count(*) * 8192) AS size
  FROM pg_buffercache b JOIN pg_class c ON b.relfilenode = pg_relation_filenode(c.oid)
 WHERE b.reldatabase = (SELECT oid FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database())
 GROUP BY c.relname ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 6;
